title: Normalization and smooth constant case
statement:
For a reduced curve, extension-invariance for $j_!\underline{\mathbf F_\ell}$
reduces through the finite normalization to the corresponding calculation on
a smooth curve, both for proper and affine opens and also when
$\ell=\operatorname{char}k$. More precisely, let k be algebraically closed, X a reduced separated finite-type k-scheme of dimension at most one, ν:Y→X its finite smooth normalization, j:U→X open and j′:Y×_X U→Y its pullback. For any prime ℓ, if the eight conditional assertions [def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions] hold for (Y,j′_!F_ℓ), then they hold for (X,j_!F_ℓ). Here no restriction ℓ≠char(k) is imposed; extension-invariance retains the prime-to-characteristic or properness conditions of C6/C7.

proof.text: Fix an algebraically closed field k, a reduced separated finite-type k-scheme X of dimension at most one, an open j:U→X, and a prime ℓ. Take ν:Y→X to be the normalization. The reduced-curve normalization lemma provides a smooth separated finite-type Y of dimension at most one, a finite ν, and a dense open V over which ν is an isomorphism. Write U′=Y×_X U and j′:U′→Y. These data include empty and zero-dimensional components.

Put R=ULift(Z/ℓZ). Since ℓ=0 in R, R/(ℓ)=R canonically, with underlying abelian group F_ℓ. The corresponding smooth calculation in this reduction is the assumption that all eight conditional assertions hold for F′=j′_!F_ℓ on Y. It is this assumption that the reduction transfers, not an assertion proved using this same reduction. We write the prime-field coefficients as R-modules; the canonical identification R/(ℓ)=R is scalarwise the identity, so the sheaves and their pullback comparison maps are the same. This reduction applies with this input in either characteristic branch.

Set F=j_!F_ℓ and G=ν_*F′. Finite pushforward transfers all eight conditional assertions from (Y,F′) to (X,G). This is the module-valued finite-pushforward assertion, applied with coefficient ring R. No identification of module constructibility with constructibility for arbitrary infinite coefficient rings is made.

The normalization exact-sequence node supplies a natural monomorphism α:F→G with constructible cokernel Q supported on the finite nonnormal locus; over the dense normal isomorphism locus V its restriction is zero. It also supplies compatibility of this sequence, its boundary maps and its open restrictions with algebraically closed field extension. These are assertions of that node, not consequences inferred just from the existence of an unspecified monomorphism.

The field k is Noetherian since its ideals are 0 and k, so Spec k is Noetherian; finite type gives Noetherian X. Apply finite-pushforward-open-quotient-constant with coefficient ring R, quotient R/(ℓ)=R (a finite set), finite map ν and open j′. This proves G constructible as an underlying sheaf of sets. For each finite locally constant stratum of G, apply finite-local-abelian-forget to its underlying abelian sheaf; this supplies additive local trivializations and finite geometric stalks. Then apply finite-local-cyclic-module-forget with n=ℓ to its restricted R-module sheaf to obtain finite constant R-module values. These are exactly the stratumwise witnesses in def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf. The constructible Q from step 4 has the same module constructibility: apply these two lemmas on its finite locally constant strata (the first is unnecessary if its constructibility is already read in abelian sheaves). Thus G and Q are constructible R-module sheaves. Here ℓ≥1 by primality, and empty strata are allowed by both lemmas. Moreover ℓ times id G is zero: every section is an R-module, and the scalar ℓ is zero in R. The same holds for Q. Thus α, G, Q and V satisfy every hypothesis of the finite-support-monomorphism assertion with coefficient ring R.

Apply the finite-support-monomorphism assertion to α. The eight assertions for G obtained in step 3 imply all eight for F. In particular it gives the actual canonical algebraically closed field-extension comparison in C6 when ℓ is prime to the characteristic and in C7 for proper X, including degrees zero and one, and gives the open-restriction surjection C8. No unconditional extension-invariance is claimed for an affine curve with characteristic-primary coefficients. For the proper and affine vanishing/finite branches on the normalization, finite-morphism permanence gives respectively proper Y over k and affine Y when X is affine. Thus the argument covers both geometric branches and both characteristic cases of the blueprint.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $X$ be a reduced separated curve of finite type over an algebraically
closed field $k$, let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be an open immersion, and let
$\ell$ be a prime (possibly $\ell=\operatorname{char}k$). Then all applicable
assertions among the eight curve assertions $\mathcal C_1,\dots,\mathcal C_8$
(vanishing, finiteness, invariance under algebraically closed extension of
$k$, and surjectivity of $H^2$ onto opens)
hold for the sheaf $j_!\underline{\mathbf F_\ell}$ on $X$.

proof.text:
Let $
u:X^
u	o X$ be the finite normalization and $j^
u:U^
u\hookrightarrow X^
u$
the pullback of $j$. The normalization $X^
u$ is a finite disjoint union of smooth curves and
points. On a component disjoint from $U^
u$ the extension-by-zero sheaf is
zero and every assertion is immediate; on every other component $U^
u$ is
dense. The dense-open localization lemma on $X^
u$ therefore reduces
$j^
u_!\underline{\mathbf F_\ell}$ to the constant sheaf on each remaining
smooth component, with the five-term sequence and all comparison maps
already specified there. If $\ell
e\operatorname{char}k$, apply the Kummer and
localization calculation; if $\ell=\operatorname{char}k$, apply the
Artin–Schreier calculation. Thus all applicable eight assertions hold for
$j^
u_!\underline{\mathbf F_\ell}$.

Exact finite direct image transfers them to
$\nu_*j^\nu_!\underline{\mathbf F_\ell}$. The normalization exact sequence
then transfers them to $j_!\underline{\mathbf F_\ell}$, including the
low-degree comparison maps and assertion (8). Properness is preserved by
finite normalization; affineness is preserved because a finite morphism
over an affine is affine. This completes the normalization, proper/affine
localization, prime-to-characteristic, and characteristic-$\ell$ branches.
